A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViGoRL research. All 31 pages of v2 and 30 pages of v3, including Appendix A1–A9, provide readable text, equations, tables and figures sufficient for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark experiments, ablations, behavioral analyses and a human evaluation in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark results, ablations, behavioral analyses and human-study outcomes.

M1.justification: Sections 4 and A5 retain the same grounded reasoning representation, MCTS-generated warm start, GRPO objectives, crop feedback procedure and multi-turn rewards.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is unchanged. Both versions include spatial reasoning, GUI grounding, web interaction and visual search, alongside ScreenSpot-Pro-LR and the appendix MMMU/RealWorldQA evaluations.

E2.justification: The comparator membership in corresponding main and appendix tables is unchanged, including SFT-direct, vanilla GRPO, external models and the Qwen2.5-VL-72B teacher comparison. Bibliographic revisions do not introduce different evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices A5–A7 retain the same data splits, sample sizes, image preprocessing, model sizes, training budgets, decoding settings, metrics and human-study procedures.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component ablations, diversity-reward analysis, point-versus-box comparison, combined-training experiment, reward comparison and error analyses. The appendix failure cases and reasoning examples are also retained.

E5.justification: Confidence-interval reporting in the result tables and human evaluation is unchanged. Neither version adds or revises seed information, repeated-run disclosures or statistical estimation procedures relative to the other.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. Examples retained in both versions include ViGoRL-3B's 62.9% SAT-2 accuracy in Table 2, multi-turn ViGoRL-7B's 86.4% on V*Bench in Table 3, and 23.72% on ScreenSpot-Pro-LR in Table A6.

T1.justification: The policy factorizations, grounded-step definition, reward definitions, GRPO loss and MCTS selection formula in Sections 3–4 and Appendix A5 are unchanged. No mathematical argument or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about grounded reasoning, multi-turn visual feedback, generalization and interpretability. Reported headline performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: The interpretations of grounding and cognitive behaviors remain unchanged. Appendix A2 retains the same limitations concerning reward hacking, excessive reasoning, restricted tool use and unresolved internal attention mechanisms.

D1.justification: The hardware disclosure, hyperparameter Tables A1–A4, MCTS implementation, study instructions and prompt Listings A1–A2 are retained. The project's access address is also unchanged.

R1.justification: Matching works across revised titles and author metadata reveals no expansion of literature coverage or substantive change in novelty positioning. Duplicate references are consolidated, and Ghosh et al. remains discussed in Appendix A4 despite its citation being removed from the introduction.

P1.justification: v3 revises bibliographic metadata and citation numbering, consolidates duplicate Visual Sketchpad, UI-R1 and Kimi k1.5 entries, and changes the Appendix A4 attribution from Gupta et al. to Akula et al. The narrative and section organization otherwise remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: Spacing around result tables and figures changes text flow, and references begin on the conclusion page in v3 rather than on a separate following page. Appendix material is repaginated, while figure content, table structures and captions are retained.

improvement.justification: The clearest gain is editorial: v3 consolidates demonstrably duplicate references for Visual Sketchpad, UI-R1 and Kimi k1.5 and tightens document layout. This modestly improves reference-list clarity and presentation. The methods, empirical evidence and scientific limitations remain unchanged.
